title: -replace and -target: emergency tools
summary: Rebuild one object on purpose with -replace (the modern taint), and why -target is for emergencies only: what it skips, the warning it prints, and the clean-up plan that must follow.

steps.title: Rebuild one thing: -replace
body: Sometimes an object must be rebuilt although the code did not change: a leaked key, a server that is broken inside,
a certificate to re-issue now.
```bash
terraform plan -replace=tls_private_key.deploy -out=tfplan   # shows -/+ ... will be replaced, as requested
terraform apply tfplan
Everything that depends on the replaced object follows through the graph (a file holding its public key, an instance
using the new AMI). `-replace` replaced `terraform taint`, which marked the object in the state at once with no
plan to review; `taint` still exists but is deprecated. A resource is also *tainted* automatically when
its creation fails half way: the next plan replaces it (`untaint` if you have fixed it by hand).

steps.title: Rotate the leaked deploy key
prompt: SEC-301 (`~/infra/deploy/TICKET.txt`): the deploy private key leaked. Rotate it **now**, and make sure the servers'
`authorized_keys` gets the new public key. Nothing else may change (the server keeps its name and its motd).

checks.name: the key is new
checks.cmd: cd ~/infra/deploy && ! terraform state show -no-color tls_private_key.deploy | grep -q "$(cat /opt/dojo/state/key)"
checks.fail: `tls_private_key.deploy` still has the leaked key. `terraform plan -replace=tls_private_key.deploy -out=tfplan`, then apply it.

checks.name: authorized_keys has the new public key
checks.cmd: cd ~/infra/deploy && diff <(terraform show -json | jq -j '.values.root_module.resources[] | select(.address == "tls_private_key.deploy") | .values.public_key_openssh') out/authorized_keys

checks.name: nothing else changed
checks.cmd: cd ~/infra/deploy && terraform state show -no-color random_pet.server | grep -q "$(cat /opt/dojo/state/pet)" && test "$(stat -c %Y out/motd.txt)" = "$(cat /opt/dojo/state/motd)" && terraform plan -detailed-exitcode -input=false -no-color >/dev/null
checks.fail: The server name or the motd changed, or the plan is not clean. Only the key (and what uses it) should be replaced.

hints: Changing the code is not needed: `-replace=ADDRESS` asks for a rebuild of one object.
`terraform plan -replace=tls_private_key.deploy -out=tfplan`: the key is replaced *as requested*, and `authorized_keys` because its content changes.
`terraform apply tfplan`, then `terraform plan` once more to see it clean.
steps.explain: One flag, a reviewable plan, and the graph did the rest. Rotation is not finished until the old key is useless everywhere: here `authorized_keys` was rewritten; in real life you would also check that nothing else (a CI secret, a vault entry) still holds the old one.

steps.title: -target: for emergencies only
body: `-target=ADDRESS` plans and applies **only** that object and what it depends on:
```text
$ terraform apply -target=aws_security_group.web
Warning: Resource targeting is in effect
You are creating a plan with the -target option, which means that the result of this plan may not
represent all of the changes requested by the current configuration.
The -target option is not for routine use, and is provided only for exceptional situations such as
recovering from errors or mistakes, or when Terraform specifically suggests to use it as part of an
error message.
Legitimate uses: an outage where one fix must go out while another part of the plan is broken; a provider error
that tells you to; bootstrapping something another resource's `for_each` needs. Every targeted apply leaves the rest
of the configuration **unapplied**, so it must be followed by a full plan and apply (or a clear note why not).
Teams that "always target" end up with states nobody can plan in one go. OpenTofu also has `-exclude=ADDRESS`, the
opposite: everything except that object.

steps.prompt: During an incident you ran `terraform apply -target=aws_security_group.web` to open a port fast. What must happen next?
options: A full `terraform plan` (and apply, once safe) so the rest of the configuration is applied too, and the fix is in the code if it was not
Nothing: the targeted apply updated the whole state
Run `-target` for every other resource, one by one
Delete the state, the targeted apply made it inconsistent
steps.explain: The state is consistent, but other pending changes in the code were skipped and are still pending. A full plan right after the incident shows what is left, while everyone still remembers why.

steps.prompt: Match the situation to the tool.
pairs: a leaked key must be rebuilt now
an outage fix must go out while another part of the plan errors
a half-created resource was fixed by hand
OpenTofu: apply everything except one broken module
